Zeroing is really quite simple.

Shoot some paper and get a reasonably tight group. Measure how far away it was from the bullseye, do some simple math and twist the little knobs appropriately.

If you need to drift your sights, make a pencil mark so you can see how far they move, do the math, and tap them until they move as far as you want.

The only complication comes from deciding what range to zero it to, and that depends on what kind of shooting you're doing, and on your personal taste. There are various charts on line for all the common calibers that will get you close enough. When in doubt, zero centerfire rifles at 100 yards, rimfires and pistols at 25.
